result.title: One Mean Log-Mel Vector per Phoneme: Simple and Fast Text Injection for Speech Recognition
result.summary: Text injection trains speech recognition models on unpaired text alongside paired audio. We feed the speech encoder synthetic input derived from text so the whole model learns from it. Previously, we synthesized this input with a frozen text-to-speech (TTS) model. Here, a simple lookup table replaces the TTS model: a mean log-mel vector (or one-hot encoding) per phoneme, repeated for a random duration drawn from alignment statistics, with silence between words. Training is 1.8 times faster than with the neural TTS, achieving comparable word error rates. With an external language model, our system reaches 1.36 / 2.90 / 1.52 / 3.24 % WER on LibriSpeech {dev,test}-{clean,other}, to our knowledge state-of-the-art using only LibriSpeech paired data, text, and lexicon. We analyze components of synthetic input (durations, acoustic features), compare different HMM aligners, evaluate scaling on the 25 000 h Loquacious dataset, and show that full-encoder injection yields strong relative improvements compared to partial-encoder and decoder methods. The code of the whole pipeline behind every number in this paper is public: github.com/rwth-i6/returnn-experiments/tree/master/2026-text-injection

AI.brief_summary: 用「每个音素一个平均 log-mel 向量」的查表合成输入替代 TTS，为语音识别编码器做文本注入训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作属语音识别训练数据增强，关注合成声学输入与 WER，未涉及视觉/多模态推理的 latent 状态生成、证据使用或停止决策，缺少可供核查的 LVR 借鉴线索。
